meta.title: Git, GitHub CLI and Claude Code commands: cheatsheet
meta.description: Git, GitHub CLI and Claude Code cheatsheet: commit, rebase, reset, gh pr, slash commands and shortcuts, with examples to copy.
meta.intro: Everyday Git commands, the GitHub CLI (gh), and Claude Code's slash commands and shortcuts.
meta.card: Git, GitHub CLI (gh) and Claude Code: commands, safe undo, slash commands, shortcuts.
meta.notice: Commands that rewrite history (reset --hard, rebase, push --force) can lose work: prefer revert and --force-with-lease. Claude Code slash commands evolve: /help lists those in your version.

entries.name: git status · git diff · git log
entries.syn: git status -sb | git diff [--staged] | git log --oneline --graph
entries.desc: Repository state, changes and history.
entries.pitfall: git diff on its own ignores what is already staged: add --staged.

entries.name: git add · git commit
entries.desc: Stages, then records a change.
ex: git commit -m "fix(web): corrige le lien du pied de page"
entries.pitfall: git add -p lets you pick the hunks to commit; --amend rewrites the last commit, avoid it after a push.

entries.name: git clone · git init
entries.desc: Fetches a repository or creates one.
entries.pitfall: --depth 1 only fetches the latest state: handy for a build, not for working on history.

entries.name: git stash
entries.syn: git stash [push -m <msg>] | git stash pop | git stash list
entries.desc: Sets aside the changes in progress.
entries.pitfall: -u includes untracked files; pop applies and removes, apply applies and keeps.

entries.name: git blame · git bisect
entries.syn: git blame <file> | git bisect start / good / bad
entries.desc: Finds who changed a line, or the commit that introduced a bug.
ex: git bisect start; git bisect bad; git bisect good v1.2.0
entries.pitfall: Always finish with git bisect reset to get back to your branch.

entries.name: git switch · git branch
entries.desc: Switches, creates, lists and deletes branches (replaces git checkout for this use).
entries.pitfall: -D deletes even an unmerged branch: check with git branch --no-merged.

entries.name: git merge · git rebase
entries.desc: Brings the commits of one branch into another.
entries.pitfall: Do not rebase a branch that is already pushed and shared. On a conflict: fix, git add, git rebase --continue.

entries.name: git cherry-pick
entries.desc: Applies a specific commit to the current branch.
entries.pitfall: -x adds the original commit's reference to the message.

entries.name: git worktree
entries.desc: Works on several branches in parallel in separate folders, without stashing.

entries.name: git restore
entries.desc: Discards a file's changes (or unstages it).
entries.pitfall: Without --staged, uncommitted changes are lost for good.

entries.name: git revert
entries.desc: Undoes a commit by creating a new one, without rewriting history (safe after a push).
entries.pitfall: To undo a merge commit, you must specify the parent with -m 1.

entries.name: git reset
entries.desc: Moves the current branch to another commit.
entries.pitfall: --hard deletes local changes. Recover a lost state with git reflog.

entries.name: git reflog
entries.desc: Log of HEAD movements: lets you find a 'lost' commit.
entries.pitfall: The reflog is local and expires (90 days by default).

entries.name: git clean
entries.desc: Deletes untracked files.
entries.pitfall: Always run -n (dry run) before -f: deleted files do not go to the recycle bin.

entries.name: git fetch · git pull · git push
entries.syn: git fetch [--prune] | git pull --rebase | git push [-u origin <branche>]
entries.desc: Syncs with the remote repository.
entries.pitfall: Prefer --force-with-lease to --force: it refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.

entries.name: git remote · git config
entries.desc: Remotes and configuration.
entries.pitfall: A config without --global only applies to the current repository.

entries.name: git tag
entries.desc: Marks a release.
ex: git tag -d v1.2.0 && git push origin :refs/tags/v1.2.0
entries.pitfall: git push does not push tags: push them explicitly or with --tags.

entries.name: gh auth · repo
entries.syn: gh auth login | gh repo clone|create|view
entries.desc: Authentication and management of GitHub repositories from the command line.

entries.name: gh pr
entries.desc: Creates and manages pull requests.
entries.pitfall: gh pr create --fill reuses the title and message of the last commit.

entries.name: gh run · workflow
entries.syn: gh run list | gh run view <id> --log-failed | gh workflow run <name>
entries.desc: Follows and reruns GitHub Actions workflows.

entries.name: gh issue · api
entries.desc: Issues and direct calls to the GitHub API.

entries.name: /help · /clear · /compact
entries.desc: Help, new conversation, and a summary of the context when it gets long.
entries.pitfall: /compact summarizes the conversation to free up room; /clear starts from scratch (CLAUDE.md is reloaded).

entries.name: /init · /memory
entries.desc: Creates a CLAUDE.md for the project; edits the memory files.
entries.pitfall: CLAUDE.md is read every session: keep it short and put no secrets in it (the file is versioned).

entries.name: /model · /config · /status
entries.desc: Switches model, opens settings, shows the session state.

entries.name: /permissions · /hooks · /mcp
entries.desc: Tool permission rules, event hooks and MCP servers.
entries.pitfall: Permission rules are saved in .claude/settings.json (project) or ~/.claude/settings.json (user).

entries.name: /review · /cost · /resume
entries.desc: Code review, token usage, resuming a previous conversation.

entries.name: Shortcuts: Esc · Shift+Tab · Ctrl+C · Ctrl+R
entries.desc: Esc interrupts the current action (Esc twice: go back in the conversation). Shift+Tab switches the permission mode (including plan mode). Ctrl+C cancels. Ctrl+R searches the history.
entries.pitfall: Shortcuts depend on the terminal: /help and the documentation list those in your version.

entries.name: Input: @ · ! · #
entries.desc: @ references a file or folder, ! runs a shell command directly, # adds a note to memory.
ex: # Toujours lancer pnpm verify avant un push

entries.name: claude (CLI) : -p · --continue · --resume
entries.desc: Launches Claude Code; -p runs a single prompt and prints the result (non-interactive mode).
ex: claude -p "Résume les changements de la dernière semaine"
entries.pitfall: In -p mode, no confirmation is asked: limit the allowed tools (--allowedTools).

entries.name: Files: CLAUDE.md · .claude/settings.json · custom commands
entries.desc: CLAUDE.md holds the project's instructions; settings.json the permissions and hooks; a Markdown file in .claude/commands/ becomes a custom slash command.
entries.pitfall: settings.local.json is for your personal settings: do not version it.
